text: Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League clash between Manchester United and Aston Villa at Old Trafford.
United failed to follow up an encouraging draw away at Liverpool, losing 2-0 at West Ham on Saturday to make it four games without a win in all competitions.

Erik ten Hag's men head into this match in eighth, already eight points off the Champions League places, though a win here against a fellow European hopeful would help to improve the atmosphere surrounding the club.
Villa's run of 14 Premier League home victories was ended by struggling Sheffield United last time out, drawing 1-1 at Villa Park on Friday.
The Villans remain in third, though, and a victory here would move Unai Emery's side level on points with leaders Liverpool at the Premier League summit.
Ten Hag makes four changes from the 2-0 loss at West Ham, as Varane and Dalot return to the back four for Kambwala and Luke Shaw, the latter of whom misses out altogether with a knock.
Eriksen and Rashford come in for McTominay and Antony.
Emery goes with two alterations to his starting XI from the draw with Sheffield United.
Matty Cash misses out through suspension, with Carlos brought in to deputise as Konsa shifts across to right-back.
Dendoncker in for Diaby is the other change.
The two sets of players make their way onto the Old Trafford pitch ahead of this huge Premier League encounter.
Who will be walking away with the three points? We will find out shortly!
The hosts kick us off and we are under way in Manchester!
United have won 38 of their 56 Premier League games against Villa (13 draws, five defeats), the highest win rate of any side to have faced another at least 40 times in the competition (68 per cent).
Neither side has really been able to grasp hold of the game yet, with a couple of misplaced passes going astray in these opening exchanges.
Hojlund's first real act is to win a free-kick for his side.
He is yet to find the back of the net in the Premier League since arriving from Atalanta, but he will be hoping to end that here.
Ten minutes on the clock at Old Trafford, and we are yet to have a clear-cut chance.
There is plenty of attacking talent on show, however, so you would expect that to change soon.
The first shot on target of the contest falls to Eriksen, though his effort from just outside the box is straight down the throat of Martinez, who makes a comfortable save.
Villa have won two of their last four Premier League games against United, as many as they had in their previous 51 against them (12 defeats, 37 losses).
The game has quite an open feel at the moment, with plenty of space to attack.
The final ball has been lacking for both sides so far, though.
Rashford is constantly looking for the ball over the top, making run after run in behind the Villa defence.
The visitors are employing a very high line, and Martinez will have to be alert to come out and sweep up if Rashford manages to beat the offside trap.
Dendoncker briefly goes down in pain after being caught with a high foot by Fernandes as the two battled for possession.
The Villa man will be okay to continue, though.
GOOOAAALLL!!! VILLA ARE IN FRONT!!! After Fernandes brought down Dendoncker, the visitors have a free-kick near the touchline.
McGinn whips the free-kick in, and it somehow evades everybody in the crowded box before nestling into the back of the net! 1-0 to the visitors!
It certainly was not the prettiest of goals, but Villa will not care as they now hold a 1-0 lead at Old Trafford.
There is plenty of time left, though, and Emery will be hoping his side can keep their concentration for the remaining 67 or so minutes.
Villa have won all nine of the Premier League games in which they have taken the lead this season.
They usually go on to take maximum points when they get their noses in front.
GOOOAAALLL!!! DENDONCKER MAKES IT 2-0!!! It is another terrible goal to concede for United, as McGinn curls a deep corner to the far post.
Lenglet is in acres of space in the box to meet it, and he nods it back across goal for Dendoncker, who swings a leg at the ball and sends it into the back of the net for his first Villa goal!
Lenglet was in far too much space at the back post, and his header back into the danger area was duly finished by Dendoncker.
What a start for Villa, who must surely fancy their chances of coming away from Old Trafford with three points that will move them joint-top with Liverpool.
For United, this could get ugly if they do not sort out their defending at set-pieces.
The hosts look to hit back through Fernandes, but his dipping effort bounces well wide of the target.
Martinez has enjoyed a pretty comfortable outing to this point.
Rashford receives the ball on the edge of the box before firing goalwards, though his low shot again fails to test Martinez as the Villa goalkeeper makes a routine stop.
United need a response, and quick.
To their credit, they have shown a bit more attacking intent since Dendoncker doubled Villa's lead.
Martinez is called into action again as Rashford pulls the trigger, though the Argentina international is able to parry away from danger.
The hosts are getting closer.
This is just the third time Villa have scored more than once away to United in the Premier League after April 2009 (3-2 defeat) and December 2019 (2-2 draw).
Emery will be desperate for his team to make it to the interval with their two-goal lead intact.
A United goal before then could give the hosts a huge psychological boost ahead of the second half.
Ten Hag's men are still probing for a goal, though Villa are certainly looking a threat when they come forward on the counter.
The next goal is absolutely pivotal to the outcome of this match.
Fernandes plays a delightful sweeping pass out to his left for Rashford, who drives into the box before lashing goalwards.
His shot is really poor, though, and flies well wide of the left post.
We are into four minutes of additional time at the end of this first half.
The first booking of the game goes to Ramsey for wiping out Garnacho as United came forward.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 0-2 ASTON VILLA
The half-time whistle blows as the teams head back to the Old Trafford changing rooms with Villa 2-0 up against United.
McGinn put the visitors ahead with 21 minutes on the clock, whipping a free-kick into the penalty area.
The ball somehow evaded everybody in the crowded box before flying into the back of the net to edge Villa in front.

It was 2-0 shortly after, United again failing to deal with a set-piece as Lenglet nodded McGinn's corner back into the danger area, where Dendoncker was waiting to turn home and leave Emery's men in the ascendancy at the interval.
United have it all to do if they are to end their winless run, though there were some positive signs towards the end of that opening 45 minutes.
Getting the next goal will prove crucial if they are to find a way back into this match.
The visitors get the ball rolling again for the second half!
NO GOAL!!! Garnacho thinks he has halved the deficit as United catch Villa on the counter, with Fernandes' clever pass giving Rashford possession on the left.
He manages to get it across to Garnacho, who springs the offside trap before going around Martinez and firing home.
However, a subsequent VAR check rules that Garnacho was offside from Rashford's pass, and Villa can breathe a sigh of relief!
With the linesman not putting up his flag to rule Garnacho offside, Digne picks up an injury while trying to stop the winger scoring.
Emery will not be best pleased about that as Digne comes off for Moreno.
United have now failed to score a first-half goal in 13 of their 19 games.
Only bottom-half sides Crystal Palace (14) and Sheffield United (16) have failed to score more often in the Premier League this season.
United fans want a red card as Martinez wipes out Rashford, who was looking to latch onto Fernandes' lofted throughball.
However, the Villa goalkeeper got to the ball first, and though he did catch Rashford with his follow-through, he got enough of the ball to not be penalised.
Villa are looking pretty comfortable at the moment, with United managing just the one shot since the break.
Emery will be thrilled with his side's display to this point.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GARNACHO MAKES IT 2-1!!! United catch Villa in possession, and Fernandes plays a neat throughball into the path of Rashford.
Much like the disallowed goal moments ago, Rashford manages to pick out Garnacho, though this time the youngster manages to stay onside before firing home to cut into Villa's lead!
Rashford kept his composure to pick out Garnacho at the back post.
SAVE!!! Just moments after seeing their lead halved, Villa nearly restore their two-goal advantage through Bailey.
The Jamaica international races onto a cross from the left before firing goalwards first time, though Onana gets down well to make a vital stop!
United's defending at set-pieces again leaves much to be desired, though Luiz's header flies well over the target.
He really should have done better there with the space he was in.
WIDE! A long ball upfield from Onana is not dealt with by Moreno, and Garnacho races onto it.
The winger takes the ball into the box before firing towards goal, but he drags his effort a little and it flies wide of the target.
United scream for a penalty as Hojlund is bundled over by Carlos, though a delayed flag goes up for offside.
United are on top at the moment, growing in momentum since Garnacho's goal.
Garnacho's goal was United's first in all competitions in 439 minutes of football since McTominay's 69th-minute strike against Chelsea earlier in December.
Twenty minutes left at Old Trafford, and the hosts are pushing for a leveller.
Emery would love a third goal to calm any late nerves, though the visitors' attacking threat has dwindled in this second half.
GOOOAAALLL!!! GARNACHO LEVELS FOR UNITED!!! The youngster has done it again as he fires home his second of the game to make it 2-2! Fernandes receives the ball on the right before trying to cross.
His delivery is flicked out by a Villa defender's leg, falling straight to Garnacho, who fires goalwards.
His shot looks as if it will be saved by Martinez, but the ball takes a wicked deflection off Carlos, wrongfooting the Villa goalkeeper and flying into the back of the net!
WHAT A BLOCK! The ball is cut back for McGinn in the United box, and it looks as if he has managed to divert into the back of the net.
However, Evans somehow gets back in the nick of time to get in the way of McGinn's shot, saving a certain goal!
Fernandes receives a yellow card for dissent after furiously protesting the referee's decision not to book Luiz for getting in the way of a quick free-kick.
Carlos is booked for hauling Hojlund to the turf as the striker looked to latch onto a long punt upfield.
After Garnacho levelled, United players raced back to the centre circle to get the game restarted.
They believe they can kick on and find a winner!
Ramsey has struggled to make an impact, and he makes way for Diaby as Emery looks to freshen up his attack.
Zaniolo, who came off the bench to score a late equaliser against Sheffield United last time out, comes on for Bailey, looking to repeat his heroics.
What impact will Emery's introductions of Diaby and Zaniolo have? The Villa head coach must be frustrated at his side squandering their two-goal advantage.
Rashford, who got the assist for Garnacho's first goal, trudges off for Antony.
Mainoo looks to rally the Old Trafford crowd as he makes way for McTominay.

GOOOAAALLL!!! HOJLUND MAKES IT 3-2!!! The young striker finally has his first Premier League goal, and what a huge one it could prove to be as United complete the turnaround! A corner comes into the Villa box, and McGinn fails to deal with it as the ball comes off his thigh and into the danger area.
It sits up perfectly for Hojlund, who fires in off the post to spark wild celebrations at Old Trafford!

Garnacho is the youngest player (19 years and 178 days) to score two goals or more on Boxing Day in the Premier League, surpassing Michael Owen (20 years and 12 days against Newcastle United in 1999).
Looking to stem the massive swing in momentum, Emery brings on Iroegbunam for Dendoncker.
McGinn, whose touch teed up Hojlund to fire home, is replaced by Duran.
Konsa is booked for a late sliding challenge on Garnacho.
Having scored what could prove to be the winner, Hojlund comes off to a great reception from the home crowd.
Kambwala is on in his place as Ten Hag looks to shore up his defence.
There are a few groans around Old Trafford as the fourth official's board indicates there will be NINE minutes of added time! Can United hold on?
Garnacho looks for his hat-trick as he latches onto Fernandes' long throughball, though he is crowded out before he can find the back of the net and make the points safe.
Eriksen makes way for Gore as United look to see out these remaining minutes.
Garnacho, whose two goals hauled United back into the game before Hojlund completed the turnaround, is replaced by Hannibal.
Villa have not been able to really trouble United in this added time, though there is still enough time for the visitors to find an equaliser.
Iroegbunam hauls down Hannibal out of frustration, and United have a free-kick as precious seconds continue to tick away.
The hosts are nearly there.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 3-2 ASTON VILLA
The full-time whistle sparks jubilant celebrations at Old Trafford as United fans celebrate a magnificent 3-2 comeback victory over Villa.

They were left with it all to do as McGinn's bizarre free-kick and Dendoncker's flicked finish had the visitors two goals to the good at the break, but United's young guns managed to turn things around.
Firstly, Garnacho fired home from Rashford's low cross, before the Argentine levelled with a deflected effort.

Hojlund got the winner, taking advantage of a loose McGinn touch in the box to find the back of the net for his first Premier League goal, one that proved to be the winner as the hosts saw out the remaining minutes.
It's a huge victory for United as they end their winless run, picking up three points that move them up to sixth.
For Villa, they miss the opportunity to move level on points with leaders Liverpool, staying in third.
They will look to get back to winning ways when they host struggling Burnley on Saturday, while United will hope to win again when they travel to Nottingham Forest the same day.
That is all we have for you from Old Trafford, so thanks for your company and goodbye!
